memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Joseph went up to bury his father. All Pharaoh's officials accompanied him—the dignitaries of his court and all the dignitaries of Egypt—besides all the members of Joseph's household and his brothers and those belonging to his father's household. Only their children and their flocks and herds were left in Goshen. Chariots and horsemen also went up with him. It was a very large company." — Gen 50:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Picture it. Egyptian dignitaries, chariots, horsemen, the whole court, travelling hundreds of miles into Canaan to bury an old shepherd.

Jacob had arrived in Egypt seventeen years earlier as a starving refugee in borrowed carts. He leaves it with a state procession.

But do not miss where they are going. This vast Egyptian company is escorting Jacob back to a cave in a field in Canaan — the only piece of the promised land his family owned. All of Egypt's splendour is, without knowing it, serving God's promise. Pharaoh's chariots are helping to carry a man home to the land God swore to give his descendants.

God has a way of using powers that do not acknowledge Him to accomplish exactly what He said He would do. Cyrus would later send Israel home from exile without ever knowing the God who called him by name (Isa 45:4-5). Rome's census put a pregnant woman on the road to Bethlehem, precisely as prophecy required.

Whatever powers seem to be running the world, they are not outside God's purposes. He is not anxious about them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you view world events as outside God's reach?
2. Where have you seen God use something unlikely to accomplish His purpose?
3. What situation are you worrying about that God is not worried about?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, nothing in this world runs outside Your purposes. Steady my heart when I look at powers and events I cannot control, and help me trust that You are working. Amen.
